awards.label: Best Overall
awards.why: 800 Series Long Range, 3-way with your existing switch, a shallow 1.16 in. body, and a 5-year warranty once registered.

awards.label: Best Budget
awards.why: The cheapest 800 Series Long Range switch here, and it still works with one standard 3-way switch.

awards.label: Best for 3-Way and 4-Way
awards.why: Works with your existing switches in 3-, 4-, or 5-way setups, even when line and load are in different boxes.

awards.label: Best for Heavy Loads
awards.why: Handles up to 600 W of LED lighting and motors up to 1 HP, and runs on 120 to 277 V.

products.verdict: The switch to buy if you're building a Z-Wave house. It's small, quick to report status, and it works in a 3-way with the ordinary switch already on the wall.
pros: 800 Series chip with Z-Wave Long Range
Direct 3-way with a regular 3-way switch, no add-on needed
Only 1.16 in. deep with no heat-sink tabs, so it fits crowded multi-gang boxes
Multi-tap scene control and an adjustable LED indicator
S2 security, SmartStart pairing, and a 5-year warranty once registered
cons: 3-way wiring means rewiring both boxes exactly as the manual shows
Advanced settings need a hub that exposes Z-Wave parameters
Needs a neutral wire

products.verdict: The easiest way to make a 3-way or 4-way circuit smart. You wire it in the box with power and leave the other switches alone.
pros: Works with existing on/off switches in 3-, 4-, and 5-way setups
No rewiring of the other boxes, even if line and load are in different boxes
800 Series with Long Range support
Multicolor LED indicator and replaceable paddles in four colors
5-year warranty once registered
cons: The other switches in the circuit must be plain on/off switches, not dimmers
Voice control only through a Z-Wave hub, not directly from a smart speaker
Needs a neutral wire

products.verdict: A solid, name-brand 800 Series switch that's rated for fans and motors as well as lights. It's sold and shipped by Amazon.
pros: 800 Series with S2 security, SmartStart, and over-the-air updates
Rated for 15 A and 3/4 HP loads, including fans and pumps
Acts as a Z-Wave repeater
Sold by Amazon
cons: 3-way needs Leviton's DD0SR companion switch
The listing doesn't mention Long Range
No scene control or LED customization listed

products.verdict: Enbrighten's newest Long Range switch. It's easy to wire thanks to auto-detecting line and load terminals, and it's selling fast.
pros: Up to 1,300 ft. range when paired as Z-Wave Long Range
Works with one standard 3-way switch or up to four Enbrighten add-ons
Auto-detecting line and load terminals
20% shallower housing than earlier models
White and light almond paddles in the box
cons: Full 3-way features need Enbrighten add-on switches
Newer listing with fewer reviews than older models
Needs a neutral wire

products.verdict: The same Long Range switch in a toggle, for rooms where a paddle would look out of place.
pros: One of the few 800 Series Long Range toggle switches
Lit toggle in eight colors and four modes
Works with one standard 3-way switch or up to four add-ons
Auto-detecting line and load terminals
cons: Toggle only comes in white
Fewer reviews than older Enbrighten models
Needs a neutral wire

products.verdict: The cheapest way into 800 Series Long Range. Flying leads make it easy to connect with wire nuts.
pros: Lowest price for an 800 Series Long Range switch on this list
Up to 1,300 ft. range as Z-Wave LR
Color-coded flying leads connect with standard wire nuts
Works with one standard 3-way switch
cons: Not compatible with UltraPro add-on switches
3.9-star rating is the lowest on this list
Needs a neutral wire

products.verdict: An older, cheaper Z-Wave Plus switch that still repeats signal and works with every Z-Wave hub. Fine for a basic single-pole circuit.
pros: Lowest price on this list
Works with every Z-Wave generation and acts as a repeater
Works indoors or controls outdoor fixtures
Light almond finish is hard to find in smart switches
cons: Older Z-Wave Plus chip without Long Range
Listing doesn't cover 3-way wiring
Sold by a third-party seller

products.verdict: A heavy-duty version of the ZEN71 for big lighting loads, fans, pumps, and 277 V commercial circuits.
pros: Up to 600 W of LED lighting and motors up to 1 HP
Runs on 120 to 277 V
Direct 3-way with a regular 3-way switch
Pigtails included
Scene control and adjustable LED
cons: One leg stays hot when off, so it isn't a disconnect for service work
Costs more than the ZEN71 for a typical light
Few reviews so far

products.verdict: Built for people who automate a lot. Multi-tap scenes and a programmable RGB LED turn it into a status display and scene controller.
pros: Up to 14 scenes from taps and holds on each paddle
RGB LED can blink or glow to show alerts
800 Series with Long Range
Works with HomeSeer and Home Assistant
cons: Not compatible with SmartThings, per the listing
3-way wiring isn't covered in the listing
3.8-star rating from a small number of reviews

products.verdict: A dependable Z-Wave Plus switch from a big electrical brand, with a 4.5-star rating. It's older tech, and 3-way needs Eaton's accessory switch.
pros: 4.5-star rating
Can control up to 5 other Z-Wave Plus devices directly through association
Status LED you can dim
cons: No Long Range or 800 Series chip
3-way needs the RF9642 accessory switch
Sold by a third-party seller

avoid.flag: Battery gadget that flips your old switch, listed as a smart switch
avoid.verdict: Despite "Smart Switch" in the title, this isn't an in-wall switch. It's a battery-powered motor that clips over your existing toggle and flips it.
reasons: It runs on AA batteries that the listing estimates last 6 to 12 months, so it needs regular attention that a wired switch never does.
The listing says it only works on single switches and won't install on double or larger gangs.
Its compatibility list leans on hubs that have been discontinued, such as Vera Lite and the D-Link/Staples Connect hub.
Every wired switch on this list costs about the same and does more.
